title: Card workflow: a small manual-based lesson
goal: Learn the three-state card workflow defined by the supplied training manual. Teach only this fictional workflow and its documented examples; do not add productivity, software, psychology or industry claims.
priorKnowledge: Can read short instructions. No technical background required.
objective: Identify a card's state, apply Begin, Complete and Reset, and explain a short action sequence using the supplied manual.

sources.title: Card workflow training manual
sources.text:
Card workflow training manual. This manual defines a fictional paper-card workflow for a training exercise. These rules are the complete specification of this exercise, not a description of an external product.

A card has exactly one current state: New, Active or Done. Every card starts in New. New means work on the card has not begun. Active means work on the card has begun but has not been completed. Done means work on the card has been completed. State is recorded by writing exactly one of these three words on the card.

There are three actions: Begin, Complete and Reset. Apply actions one at a time in the stated order, using the state produced by the previous action. Begin changes New to Active. Begin leaves Active unchanged and leaves Done unchanged. Complete changes Active to Done. Complete leaves New unchanged and leaves Done unchanged. Reset changes any state to New. Thus Reset leaves New unchanged, changes Active to New, and changes Done to New. No action has any other effect in this exercise.

Transition table, with current states in the order New, Active, Done: after Begin the resulting states are Active, Active, Done; after Complete they are New, Done, Done; after Reset they are New, New, New.

Worked examples: Starting at New, Begin then Complete gives Active then Done. Starting at New, Complete then Begin gives New then Active. Starting at Done, Begin leaves the card Done. Starting at Active, Reset then Complete gives New then New. Starting at Done, Reset then Begin gives New then Active. Starting at New, Begin then Begin gives Active then Active. Starting at Active, Complete then Reset gives Done then New. Starting at New, Complete then Complete leaves the card New after each action.

To trace a sequence, record the initial state and then record the resulting state after each action. An action that leaves the state unchanged is still a step in the sequence. The two sequences Begin then Complete and Complete then Begin have different final states when starting at New: Done and Active respectively. Reset does not complete work; it returns the card to New. Completing a New card does not skip Active; it leaves the card New. Beginning a Done card does not reopen it; use Reset followed by Begin to reach Active from Done.
